heading: LESSON OBJECTIVE
text: Identify similar triangles and calculate unknown sides using corresponding ratios.

heading: CORE IDEA
text: Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles and proportional side lengths.

heading: KEY DEFINITIONS
text: A scale factor k is the image side length divided by its corresponding original side.

heading: CORE RULE
text: For ABC similar to DEF: DE/AB=EF/BC=DF/AC=k.

heading: MATCHING VERTICES
text: Read the triangle names in order: A matches D, B matches E, C matches F.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 1
text: 3–4–5 scaled by 2 becomes 6–8–10. Every matching ratio is 2.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 2
text: If 6 corresponds to 18, k=3; a matching side 7 becomes 21.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 3
text: If 4 corresponds to 10, k=2.5; then 6 corresponds to 15.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 4
text: Triangles with angles 45°,55°,80° and 45°,80°,55° are similar by AA.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 5
text: A 1.8 m person casts a 1.2 m shadow. A tree casting an 8 m shadow is 12 m tall: h/8=1.8/1.2.

heading: DETERMINISTIC DIAGRAM
text: Right triangles with legs 3,4 and 6,8 have hypotenuses 5,10. All sides scale by 2.

heading: PERIMETER AND AREA
text: Perimeter scales by k; area scales by k squared.

heading: COMMON MISTAKES
text: Do not mismatch corresponding sides, invert one ratio only, or use k instead of k squared for area.

heading: EXAM STRATEGY
text: Mark matching angles, write one consistent proportion, solve, and verify all ratios.

heading: QUICK CHECK
text: If 5 corresponds to 15, k=3; then 8 corresponds to 24 and area 12 corresponds to 108.

heading: RECAP AND NEXT STEP
text: Angles match, sides are proportional. Practice 18 problems, review answers, take the five-question test, and watch the full bilingual lesson.
